prompt: A clean, front-on photograph of a standard wall-mounted logMAR eye-test chart (the kind used by opticians), with 7 rows of black capital letters on a white chart, the top row a single large letter and each row below it holding more, smaller letters. The letter sizes follow the logMAR standard: going DOWN the chart, each row's letters are smaller than the row above by a CONSTANT ratio — every row is exactly 10^0.1 (about 1.259) times the height of the row below it, a fixed geometric shrink from row to row (NOT a constant step, and NOT a guessed amount). So the seven rows form a precise geometric progression of letter heights. A genuine chart photograph: crisp black letters, white background, even lighting, no numbers or acuity fractions printed beside the rows, no other text.
